newsitem.title: JAPAN: ASIA SUGAR-RAIN SEEN WEIGHING ON '98 THAI PREMIUMS.
newsitem.headline: ASIA SUGAR-RAIN SEEN WEIGHING ON '98 THAI PREMIUMS.

text.p: Thai raw sugar premiums for delivery next year are set to ease as the latest rain following a drought is expected to boost the country's new crop, traders in Tokyo said on Friday.
"The premiums (for 1998 deliveries) will be soft for a while," said a trader at one of Japan's major trading houses. "It's raining now. We're watching how the new crop turns out."

Traders said premiums for deliveries next year stood at around 90/100 per pound over New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange futures on an fob basis, well below an average of around 110 in term contracts for next year.
Some traders said the high level agreed in the term contracts also attracted some sugar from Cuba as well as Brazil, putting downward pressure on premiums for spot deals.
"It pays to bring sugar from those countries when the premiums stand around 100," said one trader.
Premiums for July-September deliveries stood at 80/90, although only a few deals were being struck as the business for the period was nearing an end, they said.

Asked about the financial crisis in Thailand, which is calling for the biggest international lending programme since the 1995 Mexico crisis, one sugar trader said: "They (Thai suppliers) are eager to receive dollars as early as possible. But we've seen little impact as there's little left to offer by the end of this year."
